rows.english: A super robot built through the cooperation of Dr. Ryuzaki and Dr. Izumi. It was originally a trailer for underground development that was converted into a combat robot, and uses Daimolite as its energy source. Daimolite is crystallized light born from a neutrino reaction; the light particles solidified under high gravity collide violently with one another and thereby keep emitting enormous energy. Also, Daimolite triggers a nuclear reaction and explodes massively at 4 degrees Celsius or above, and when fully released, it turns Daimos itself into a pure energy body. Because Daimos has a control system that traces the pilot's movements, it reproduces Kazuya's karate techniques without the slightest error, but conversely it has the weakness that when Daimos takes damage, the pilot takes damage too. Its weapons are mostly mid- and close-range ones such as the Five Shooter and the Triple Dragon Staff, making it a machine that emphasizes close combat. Also, the "Deadly Gale Correct Fist Thrust" was originally not a combination technique with Blizzard-type weapons but the name of the karate technique itself that delivers the finishing blow; likewise, following up from Blizzard-type weapons, it also used the "Deadly Gale Hand-Blade Thrust" and the "Deadly Daimos Chop."

However, although Terminus Energy has high output, collecting it and converting it to power was extremely difficult, and it was predicted that it would take several years to complete the TE Engine. In addition, Dr. Zapat had also succeeded in developing "Lasmunanium," an armor material capable of self-repair, but this too ran into the problem that its function was difficult to control, just like the TE Engine. After trial and error with prototype units No. 1 through No. 4, Dr. Zapat gave up on developing a machine equipped with both Lasmunanium and the TE Engine. He assigned Lasmunanium to prototype unit No. 5, "Medius Locus," and the TE Engine to prototype units No. 6 and No. 7, and decided to pursue and improve each function. Furthermore, these three machines were given concepts and armament assuming actual combat: prototype No. 6 was developed for high-mobility combat and artillery combat, prototype No. 7 for close combat and melee combat, and Medius Locus as a machine with performance intermediate between the two machines described above. This machine was the first of the three above to roll out, but no test pilot was decided, and unlike prototypes No. 6 and No. 7, almost no tests of various kinds were carried out (one theory holds that it secretly underwent some kind of modification).
